title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 20, 2026
summary: EFFIS's current-situation page now lists 669,118 hectares burned EU-wide as of 16 September — a minor upward revision of the 668,035 ha figure recorded two days ago for the same date, reflecting the agency's routine satellite-imagery refinement rather than new fire growth. Romania's energy-sector state of alert, first declared 1 August after the Cernavodă plant's first reactor shutdown, remains extended through 30 September, with both reactors still offline and Danube flow insufficient to support a restart. EFFIS's fire-danger forecast for 17-23 September continues to flag very extreme conditions across most of France, the Pyrenees and northwestern Morocco. Multi-strategy searches (topic, actor, and per-country) found no new wildfire outbreaks, fatalities or evacuations across Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Greece or Romania in the 18-20 September window, extending the quiet period first noted in mid-September.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 18, 2026
summary: EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 668,035 hectares as of 16 September, up ~1,501 hectares over one day — still well below 2025's record pace for this point in the season but nearly double the 20-year average. EFFIS's fire danger forecast for 17-23 September flags very extreme conditions across most of France, the Pyrenees and northwestern Morocco, with extreme-to-very-high danger extending across much of Iberia, the Balkans and the Caucasus/Caspian region. No new wildfire outbreaks, fatalities or evacuations were confirmed across Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Greece or Romania in the 11-18 September window, and Cernavodă's reactors remain offline as Danube flow stays insufficient for a restart.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 16, 2026
summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen used her State of the Union address in Strasbourg to call 2026 'the summer of truth,' proposing a new European Heatwave Plan and a future dedicated EU firefighting aircraft fleet, citing roughly 660,000 hectares burned, 35,000+ heat-linked deaths and about €2 billion in lost EU grain-farmer revenue this year. EFFIS separately put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 666,534 hectares as of 15 September, up ~7,115 hectares over two days — a faster pace than the prior slowdown but still well below 2025's record pace for this point in the season. No new wildfire outbreaks, fatalities or evacuations were confirmed across Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Greece or Romania, and Cernavodă's reactors remain offline pending Danube-flow recovery.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 14, 2026
summary: EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 659,419 hectares as of 13 September, up just ~1,092 hectares over three days — the slowest multi-day growth rate of the season — as fire danger continued easing broadly across the continent, though extreme conditions persisted in pockets of the western Balkans, southern Italy and Sicily. Romania's Energy Command confirmed its next Cernavodă restart assessment will come only after 15 September, with the Danube still not carrying enough water to cool either reactor and officials still targeting a restart toward the end of the month. No new wildfire outbreaks, fatalities or evacuations were confirmed across Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Greece or Romania in the multi-strategy search window.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 13, 2026
summary: The European Commission confirmed on 28 August that WWF Central and Eastern Europe filed a 2024 complaint questioning the EU-compliance of a long-delayed Danube hydrotechnical project on the Bala branch — the same works meant to raise water levels near the Cernavodă nuclear plant's cooling intake. Former Transport Minister Sorin Grindeanu blamed the complaint for leaving the project stalled as the energy crisis unfolded, a framing WWF and Greenpeace call unfounded, noting the works had been proposed 23 years earlier. EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 658,327 hectares as of 10 September, up a modest 816 hectares as fire danger eased broadly across the continent, though extreme conditions persist through 16 September across Iberia, the Pyrenees, most of France, the western Balkans, southern Italy/Sicily and eastern Turkey. No new wildfire outbreaks, fatalities or evacuations confirmed across the six tracked countries since early September; breaking status downgraded to reflect the sustained quiet period.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 11, 2026
summary: Romania's Ministry of Energy warned on 9 September that Danube inflow at the country's border could stay low throughout September, meaning Cernavodă's cooling-water level may remain insufficient to restart either reactor before October — a further slip from the 'beyond mid-September' timeline cited earlier in the month. The Joint Research Centre's EFFIS system put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 657,511 hectares as of 9 September, up modestly from 655,658 hectares the day before, still trailing 2025's record pace but nearly double the 20-year seasonal average. No new wildfire outbreaks, fatalities or evacuations were confirmed across Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Greece or Romania in the 4-11 September gap window after multi-strategy searches.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 4, 2026
summary: Romanian officials said the Cernavodă nuclear plant, offline since 13 August, will not restart before 10 September at the earliest, as Danube water levels at the plant's intake have not shown a sustained enough rise; the government's National Committee for Emergency Situations approved a new three-stage plan (repositioning barges, a modular pontoon dam, and high-capacity pumps) to raise the cooling-canal level past its 1.58m intervention trigger from the current 1.86m. EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 647,882 hectares as of 3 September — still below 2025's record pace but well above the 20-year average — and forecast extreme to very extreme fire danger returning across Iberia, France, the Alps, northern Italy, the Balkans, Greece and Ukraine for 3-9 September as hot, dry weather resurges.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 2, 2026
summary: EFFIS raised the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total to 646,628 hectares as of 1 September, up from 636,100 ha a week earlier and still well above the 20-year seasonal average despite trailing 2025's record pace. Romania's Cernavodă nuclear plant remained fully offline heading into September, with the government's energy-sector state of alert still in force through 30 September and Danube flow forecasts continuing to fluctuate between roughly 1,450 and 1,600 m3/s against a historical August average of 3,900 m3/s. No new acute wildfire outbreaks, fatalities, or evacuations were confirmed in the Aug 27-Sep 2 window across Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Greece or Romania.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 31, 2026
summary: Romania's government extended the energy sector's state of alert by a full month, from 31 August to 30 September 2026, after concluding the Danube's hydrological deficit remains too severe to restart either Cernavodă reactor; officials also cited a weaker wind/solar forecast and rising peak demand. Grid operator Transelectrica and Nuclearelectrica continued leaning on emergency power imports via Ukraine and Moldova's Energocom to cover the shortfall, first activated in early August. EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 636,100 hectares as of 30 August — still below 2025's record pace but well above the 20-year average — as a heat dome held 40-43°C highs over Italy and the Balkans through the end of the month.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 30, 2026
summary: Cernavodă's scheduled Unit 2 outage window expires at midnight with no restart yet confirmed by Nuclearelectrica, as Romania continues building a temporary guide dam on the Old Danube arm and releasing Olt River reservoir water to restore cooling flow. The EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total holds near 634,500 hectares as the sixth seasonal heat dome continues pushing 40-43°C highs into Italy and the Balkans. Backfilled reporting confirmed Serbia's Deliblato Sands wildfire — burning intermittently since 5 August in a Vojvodina nature reserve east of Belgrade — grew to more than 3,500 hectares and drew EU rescEU helicopters plus a Russian Ilyushin waterbomber before improving by 25 August, with President Vučić touring the site and no casualties reported.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 29, 2026
summary: A sixth heat dome of the season pushed into Italy and the Balkans from 27 August, driving temperatures to 42-43°C across the Po Valley, Croatia, Hungary, Serbia and Bosnia and threatening to further delay the Danube's recovery. Romania's Cernavodă nuclear plant remained fully offline as authorities raced to complete a temporary guide dam on the Old Danube arm and continued releasing water from Olt River reservoirs, with flow still holding near a third of the historical average. The EU's cumulative 2026 burned area rose to 634,473 hectares as of 27 August, with the fire-danger map continuing to shift east. Aragón's Peñas de Riglos fire, which killed a UME soldier and forced over 1,000 evacuations, was confirmed stabilized at an 18,400-hectare perimeter after the region's largest-ever firefighting mobilization.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: Belgium's largest wildfire on record burned roughly 3,000 hectares in the High Fens and pushed smoke toward Germany, while a Spanish UME soldier was killed fighting Aragón's 16,600-hectare Peñas de Riglos fire, which also forced 1,045 evacuations. Greece evacuated 481 people by sea from a Halkidiki blaze, and a second Landes fire near Luglon burned 1,700 hectares before being contained. Romania restarted a 300 MW coal unit at Rovinari and unblocked the long-delayed Bala 2 project to secure future Danube cooling water, as both Cernavodă reactors remained offline. EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 burned area at 619,613 hectares, still below 2025's record pace, while a new Bloomberg tally put Europe-wide heat deaths above 25,000 since April.
